events.title: Flohmarkt am Naschmarkt
events.description: Vienna’s big weekly flea market, at the far end of the Naschmarkt food market. Old furniture, records, glassware, postcards and plenty of junk.
events.why: A real Saturday-morning habit for locals. Go early for the best finds, then have breakfast at one of the market’s cafés.

events.title: Bauernmarkt am Karmelitermarkt
events.description: One of Vienna’s biggest farmers’ markets, across the canal from the old town in Leopoldstadt. Regional meat, sausage and seasonal fruit and vegetables.
events.why: A neighbourhood market where locals actually shop, with good cafés around the square.

events.title: Biomarkt Freyung
events.description: A small organic farmers’ market on a square in the old town, selling bread, cheese, vegetables and other local produce.
events.why: An easy, low-key look at what Austrian farmers grow, right in the centre. Good for picnic food.

events.title: Lebt und arbeitet in Wien
events.description: A big group show of art by people who live and work in Vienna today: more than 130 works of painting, sculpture, video and more, at two sites of the city’s contemporary art hall.
events.why: Last chance, and entry is free on Sunday Oct 25. A quick look at what the city’s artists are making right now.

events.title: Tolia Astakhishvili: Figure of the Child
events.description: A solo show by a contemporary artist from Georgia, at Vienna’s museum of modern art in the MuseumsQuartier, the big museum complex just outside the old town.
events.why: Last chance to see it before it closes on Nov 1.

events.title: Bernhard Leitner: SOUNDSPACESCULPTURE
events.description: An exhibition where sound is the material: a Viennese artist uses speakers and moving sound to shape the space you walk through. Two other artists show alongside him.
events.why: The same ticket gets you into the basement room with Klimt’s Beethoven Frieze, a famous wall painting from 1902.

events.title: Erika Giovanna Klien: All Is Movement
events.description: Paintings and drawings by a Viennese artist of the 1920s who tried to show movement and speed on paper and canvas, part of a short-lived local avant-garde.
events.why: A side of 1920s Vienna few visitors see, a short walk through the garden from the Belvedere’s famous Klimts.

events.title: 20 Years of Vienna Design Week: A City Full of Posters
events.description: Twenty years of posters from Vienna Design Week, the city’s yearly design festival, at the museum of design and decorative arts.
events.why: Last chance. A quick, colourful look at the city’s design scene, easy to pair with the museum’s rooms of Vienna 1900 furniture.

events.title: Der fliegende Holländer
events.description: Wagner’s opera The Flying Dutchman: a ghostly sea captain is doomed to sail forever unless a woman stays faithful to him. Stormy, dramatic music.
events.why: Wagner in a small, historic theatre, much closer to the stage than at the big State Opera.
events.language: Sung in German, subtitles not confirmed

events.title: Fink
events.description: A British band led by singer-songwriter Fin Greenall, playing slow-burning songs that mix folk, blues and electronic sounds.
events.why: A good way to see Arena, a rock venue in a former slaughterhouse that’s popular with locals.

events.title: Nijinsky
events.description: A new ballet about Vaslav Nijinsky, a famous early 20th-century dancer whose career ended in mental illness. Told through big, dramatic dancing.
events.why: The State Ballet’s big new show of the autumn. Opening night is also streamed online if you can’t get a seat.

events.title: Die Fledermaus
events.description: Vienna’s best-loved operetta, a light comedy with songs about a revenge prank played out at a masked ball. Waltzes, champagne and mistaken identities.
events.why: The classic Viennese night out, at the theatre that has played it for decades, with English surtitles.

events.title: Hercules
events.description: Handel’s drama about the hero Hercules and his jealous wife, who sends him a robe she thinks will win back his love. It kills him instead.
events.why: A single night of baroque opera, music from the 1700s, which this small theatre does especially well.

events.title: New York Philharmonic with Gustavo Dudamel
events.description: One of America’s great orchestras on tour, two nights in a row. The first night ends with a Mahler symphony, the second mixes new American music with Prokofiev.
events.why: A chance to hear a top orchestra in the Musikverein’s main hall, one of the best-sounding concert halls in the world.
events.dateNote: Also Oct 22, with a different programme

events.title: Viennale
events.description: Vienna’s big film festival: two weeks of new films from around the world, an old-Hollywood retrospective, talks with filmmakers and late-night parties.
events.why: The city’s main cultural event of the autumn. If a screening is sold out, check the festival’s page for returned tickets.

events.title: Robert Aldrich retrospective
events.description: A season of tough, stylish Hollywood films from the 1950s to the 1970s by one director, including the war film The Dirty Dozen, at the city’s film museum.
events.why: Almost every screening starts with a short live introduction, and it runs on for two weeks after the festival.

events.title: Friday Afternoon
events.titleEnglish: Vienna Boys’ Choir: Friday afternoon concert
events.description: A relaxed concert by the Vienna Boys’ Choir in their own hall by the Augarten park: Haydn, Mozart, Schubert and Strauss, plus some folk and pop.
events.why: An easier way to hear the choir than the Sunday mass, with proper seats and a short, mixed programme.

events.title: Vienna 1900: guided tour in English
events.description: A guided tour in English through rooms of Viennese furniture, glass and household design from around 1900, when the city set new standards for modern design.
events.why: An easy, guided way into Vienna 1900 design, with someone to explain what you’re looking at.

events.title: Das Ferienhaus
events.description: A modern family drama based on a classic play by Ibsen, set at a holiday house, on the main stage of Vienna’s national theatre.
events.why: One of the few evenings at the national theatre where you can follow along with surtitles on your phone.
events.language: In German, with phone surtitles (English not confirmed)

events.title: L’Orfeo
events.description: One of the very first operas ever written, from 1607: the myth of Orpheus, who goes down to the underworld to bring back his dead wife.
events.why: A chance to hear how opera began, in one of the world’s grandest opera houses.
events.language: Sung in Italian, subtitles not confirmed

events.title: Krystian Zimerman piano recital
events.description: A solo piano recital by one of the world’s most admired pianists, who plays few concerts and rarely records.
events.why: He tours very little, so this is a rare chance to hear him live. Only the last tickets are left.

events.title: Sonntagsmesse der Wiener Sängerknaben
events.venueNote: the chapel in the old palace
events.description: The famous boys’ choir sings Sunday mass in the small royal chapel of the Hofburg, the old imperial palace in the city centre.
events.why: The way to hear the choir where it has sung for centuries, as part of a real church service rather than a concert.

events.title: Otello
events.description: Verdi’s opera of Shakespeare’s Othello, a story of jealousy and betrayal, with Jonas Kaufmann, one of the world’s best-known tenors, in the title role.
events.why: Kaufmann is listed for all five nights, and seats go fast, so book early.
events.language: Sung in Italian, subtitles not confirmed

events.title: Nationalfeiertag
events.description: Austria’s national holiday. The army usually sets up displays on Heldenplatz, the big square by the old palace, and police and fire services show their work at City Hall.
events.why: This is how Viennese families spend the day, strolling among tanks and fire engines. Many shops close, so plan ahead.

events.title: Wir sind noch einmal davongekommen
events.description: Thornton Wilder’s The Skin of Our Teeth, an American comedy about one family that survives the ice age, a great flood and war, played in German.
events.why: A play many English speakers know, so it’s easy to follow, with surtitles on your phone.
events.language: In German, with phone surtitles (English not confirmed)

events.title: Die letzten Tage der Menschheit
events.description: A huge, biting satire of Vienna during the First World War, “The Last Days of Mankind”, written by the city’s most famous critic and long thought impossible to stage.
events.why: A big Viennese classic, made easier with phone surtitles, and some €25 tickets on Oct 30.
events.language: In German, with phone surtitles (English not confirmed)

events.title: Wien Modern
events.description: A month of new and experimental music in concert halls, clubs and churches around the city. Expect anything from orchestras to sound installations.
events.why: A different side of musical Vienna, often in unusual places, with top orchestras and ensembles.

events.title: Musikverein Perspektiven: Elfriede Jelinek
events.description: Five days of concerts, readings, films and talks about Elfriede Jelinek, the Austrian novelist who won the Nobel Prize, plus a sound and video installation.
events.why: On Nov 4, two of Austria’s best-loved actors read on stage.

events.title: Talk with Volker Schlöndorff
events.description: A talk with Volker Schlöndorff, the German director of The Tin Drum, a 1979 film that won both the top prize at Cannes and an Oscar.
events.why: A chance to hear a key figure of German film in person.
events.venueNote: festival centre in the old radio building

events.title: La Fille du régiment
events.description: A comic opera about a girl raised by a regiment of soldiers. It’s short, funny and a gentle first opera.
events.why: A light evening if you’ve never been to an opera, and an easy break from the heavier works this month.
events.language: Sung in French, subtitles not confirmed

events.title: Ernst Molden & Der Nino aus Wien
events.description: Two Viennese songwriters, one older and one younger, singing their own songs about Austria in the local dialect, in the tradition of the Wienerlied (Viennese song).
events.why: Music that locals actually listen to, in a proper concert hall.

events.title: Christmas Market at Schönbrunn Palace
events.description: A Christmas market in front of Schönbrunn, the emperors’ summer palace, and one of the first in the city to open.
events.why: Opens before most other markets, so you get the mulled wine and the palace view without the December crowds.

events.title: Blickfang
events.description: A design fair where about 160 selected designers sell their own furniture, lamps, clothes and jewellery, at the museum of design and decorative arts.
events.why: You can buy straight from the people who made it, and chat with them while you do.

events.title: Bill Frisell Trio
events.description: A trio led by an American jazz guitarist who blends jazz with country and folk. Warm, melodic music, mostly without words.
events.why: A guitarist who usually plays much bigger halls, in Vienna’s main jazz club.

events.title: Franz West: The Revolution of Sculpture
events.description: A big show of a Viennese artist known for lumpy, odd sculptures you were often allowed to sit on or handle, at the modern branch of the Albertina museum.
events.why: The autumn’s big exhibition on one of Vienna’s own artists, opening this week.

events.title: Imperial Lights
events.description: A walk-through light show in the gardens of Schönbrunn Palace, with lit-up figures and decorations in the style of the palace.
events.why: Easy to combine with the palace Christmas market on the same evening.

events.title: Vienna Art Week
events.description: A week of free tours, talks, open studios and exhibitions with around 70 museums, galleries and art schools across the city.
events.why: It’s free, and the open studio days get you into artists’ workspaces you couldn’t otherwise see.

events.title: Hotel Savoy
events.description: A stage version of a 1924 novel about a soldier coming home from the war to a grand hotel, told with a live band that mixes brass music and old songs.
events.why: Lots of live music, so the evening still works if your German is patchy. This is the opening night.

events.title: Lise Davidsen sings Schubert
events.description: Lise Davidsen, one of today’s most talked-about opera singers, sings Schubert’s songs with piano, in Vienna’s grand concert hall.
events.why: A huge opera voice in an intimate set of songs, in the city where Schubert wrote them.

events.title: Simon Keenlyside recital
events.description: An English baritone sings an evening of songs with piano, on the main stage of the State Opera.
events.why: A rare quiet evening of songs inside the grand opera house.

events.title: Art&Antique
events.description: An art and antiques fair with dealers from Austria and abroad, from ancient objects to modern design, inside the old imperial palace.
events.why: A chance to browse old Viennese furniture and design in the palace’s grand halls, whether or not you buy.

events.title: Viennese Christmas Market at Rathausplatz
events.description: The city’s biggest Christmas market, in front of the City Hall, with skating paths winding through the park beside it.
events.why: Go in the first week, before the coach tours arrive.

events.title: Old Viennese Christmas Market
events.description: A traditional Christmas market on an old square in the centre, selling handmade crafts, glass ornaments, nativity figures and pottery.
events.why: The old-fashioned choice in the city centre, with live Christmas music in the late afternoons.

events.title: Kunst & Design Markt
events.description: A market of small local designers and makers selling clothes, jewellery, homeware, chocolate and more, inside a working brewery.
events.why: Early Christmas shopping from local makers, in one of Vienna’s last big breweries.
